strategy.summary: pandas PR #68688 fixes _astype_nansafe so object-dtype numeric input cast to timedelta64 with a unit (m8[s], m8[ms]) is interpreted in that unit instead of nanoseconds; the buggy code calls array_to_timedelta64 with no unit and casts the ns result, so pd.Series([2,3],dtype=object).astype('m8[s]') yields zeros. The reproducing tests are in pandas/tests/series/methods/test_astype.py and pandas/tests/frame/methods/test_astype.py.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) capable of building pandas Cython extensions
pinned_because: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have no documented constraint and no era table entry in the context, so no version is pinned; the build uses whatever versions the current pandas build requires, which is an unverified choice and is stated here rather than inferred from era
Python version not stated by the evidence (null), so it is left to the environment default supported by the buggy commit's pyproject

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/series/methods/test_astype.py -k 'test_astype_object_numeric_to_timedelta64_unit or test_astype_object_to_timedelta64_unit_numeric_only or test_astype_object_to_datetimelike_no_unit' pandas/tests/frame/methods/test_astype.py -k 'test_astype_object_numeric_to_timedelta64_unit_2d or test_astype_from_object_to_timedelta_unit' -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/series/methods/test_astype.py::test_astype_object_numeric_to_timedelta64_unit[s] (parametrized over s, ms, us, ns) and pandas/tests/frame/methods/test_astype.py::test_astype_object_numeric_to_timedelta64_unit_2d, plus test_astype_object_to_timedelta64_unit_numeric_only and test_astype_object_numeric_to_timedelta64_unit_2d_mixed
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision 7cafb46e9665 the unit-specific series test for m8[s] (ser.astype('m8[s]') compared with pd.Series([2,3],dtype='m8[s]')) and the 2D frame test fail because the astype result is all zeros (values read as nanoseconds); on the fixed PR revision the same tests pass because the timedelta64 branch delegates to TimedeltaArray._from_sequence with the unit, matching the constructor. Success is only this fail-to-pass transition, not any printed value.
strategy.numerical_probe: pd.Series([2, 3], dtype=object).astype('m8[s]') should differ from pd.Series([2, 3], dtype='m8[s]') on the buggy revision (zeros vs 2s and 3s) and agree on the fixed revision.
risks: The defect is a value-level transition with no platform dependence stated in the evidence, so it should reproduce on Linux x86_64 with a standard build; no architecture or sanitizer requirement is documented, and none is assumed.

Dependency versions for NumPy, dateutil, tzdata and Cython are unbounded in the evidence; a NumPy version mismatch with the buggy commit could alter array_to_timedelta64 behaviour or cause build failures, and this plan does not verify it.

The frame test uses a 2D object block; whether df.astype takes the same path depends on block layout in the buggy commit, so the test asserts len(df._mgr.blocks)==1 and the mixed-string case must be checked on both revisions.

The test diff also changes unrelated error-message expectations (test_astype_from_object_to_timedelta_unit and test_merge test_other_timedelta_unit); those may fail on the buggy revision for message wording reasons rather than the numerical bug, so they are not part of the numerical transition and should be excluded from judgement of the fix.
Built editable install must be rebuilt after checking out each revision; a stale Cython build from the other revision would invalidate the transition.

oracle.reference_source: pd.Series(values, dtype='m8[unit]') constructor behaviour, as stated in the PR test
oracle.why: The tests compare astype results against the constructor with assert_series_equal, which is exact for integer-valued timedelta64 results.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On revision 7cafb46e9665, ser.astype('m8[s]') returns zeros where the constructor gives 2s and 3s, so tm.assert_series_equal raises AssertionError because the timedelta values differ; the 2D frame test fails the same way.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the timedelta64 branch of _astype_nansafe delegates to TimedeltaArray._from_sequence with the requested unit, so astype equals the constructor result and assert_series_equal/assert_frame_equal pass.
